This market will resolve to the temperature range that contains the highest temperature recorded by NOAA at the Hartsfield-Jackson International Airport Station in degrees Fahrenheit on 31 Aug '26.

The resolution source for this market will be information from NOAA, specifically the highest reading under the "Temp" column for all times on this day, available here: https://www.weather.gov/wrh/timeseries?site=katl

This market will resolve off of the Hourly Data provided using the "Show Hourly Data" button.

If NOAA data for the observation date is unavailable by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, the Weather Underground Daily Observations table will be used as the resolution source.

In the event which there is no data for the observation date by 11:59 PM ET on the day following the observation date, this market will resolve to the lowest bracket.

To toggle between Fahrenheit and Celsius, click the "Switch to US Units w/ kts" button until the relevant table displays °F.

This market can not resolve until the first data point for the following date has been published on the resolution source.

The resolution source for this market measures temperatures to whole degrees Fahrenheit (eg, 21°F). Thus, this is the level of precision that will be used when resolving the market.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description: Official National Weather Service observations and station data confirm Atlanta reached a daily maximum of 92–93°F on August 31 under clear, sunny skies with light winds, consistent with NWS forecasts issued that morning. A dominant high-pressure ridge promoted strong solar heating and minimal cloud cover, pushing temperatures above the 1991–2020 average high of 87°F amid an ongoing late-summer warm pattern. Trader consensus at 100% reflects this verified outcome from official reporting. Only unexpected afternoon convection or measurement revisions at key airports could have shifted the result outside that narrow range, though neither materialized.

eventMetadata.context_description: Strong consensus among weather models and Central Weather Administration forecasts supports the near-certain 32°C outcome for Taipei’s September 1 maximum, with expected highs of 31–32°C amid widespread cloud cover, easterly flow, and frequent showers or thunderstorms that suppress daytime heating. September climatology features average highs near 30–31°C with high humidity and monsoon influences, aligning closely with current guidance showing limited solar insolation. Real-time observations and short-range runs indicate peak temperatures will likely occur midday before convective activity intensifies. The dominant market-implied odds reflect this tight scientific agreement, though brief clearing or delayed rainfall timing could allow brief spikes toward 33–34°C, while heavier or earlier precipitation might cap readings at 30–31°C.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Trader sentiment on the Kuala Lumpur highest-temperature market for September 1, 2026, centers on 32°C and 33°C as the clear leaders (combined ~95.6% implied probability) because official forecasts and climatological norms point to a typical equatorial September daytime maximum in that narrow band.**

Kuala Lumpur’s tropical climate produces consistent highs near 32–33°C during the inter-monsoon period, moderated by high humidity, frequent afternoon convection, and cloud cover that limits radiative heating. Malaysian Meteorological Department guidance and multiple numerical models (including those referenced in WeatherBug, Met Office, and regional outlooks) currently indicate a high of 31–34°C, with many runs clustering at 31–33°C and thunderstorms expected to develop by midday or afternoon—conditions that historically cap peaks below 34°C on most September days. 

The low 7% odds on 34°C reflect residual uncertainty around exact rain timing and any brief clearing that could allow an extra degree or two, while probabilities collapse beyond 35°C or below 31°C because those outcomes lie well outside both recent model consensus and the long-term September distribution (mean daily maximum ~32–33°C). Traders are therefore pricing the market-implied odds around the most probable outcomes supported by current forecast guidance rather than extremes.

Updated model runs and official briefings over the next 24 hours will provide the final refinement ahead of the daily maximum observation.

Revisions to temperatures recorded within this market's timeframe will be considered until the first datapoint for the following date has been published, after which any alterations will not be considered.

eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast consensus points to a maximum of 20–22 °C in Moscow on September 2, 2026, aligning with the market’s heaviest weighting on 21 °C (48.5 %).** Multiple numerical weather prediction outputs and official guidance issued in the final days of August show a transition from the warmer air mass that produced highs near 25–27 °C on August 31–September 1. A southwesterly flow ahead of an approaching trough is expected to advect cooler maritime air, increase cloud cover, and introduce a modest chance of light showers, limiting daytime heating.

Model runs place the daily maximum between roughly 20 °C and 22 °C, with 21 °C appearing most frequently. Historical climatology for early September (typical highs 18–20 °C) supports the view that this will be a near-normal rather than anomalously warm day. Because resolution hinges on the official observed maximum, traders are closely tracking the latest model updates and any revisions to the 12–18 UTC temperature guidance, which could shift probabilities between the tightly bunched 20–22 °C outcomes.

Final NWP updates and real-time observations tomorrow will resolve the narrow range.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent forecasts from multiple models converge on a daily maximum near 36–37°C for Jeddah on September 2, driven by persistent northwest winds, clear skies, and high-pressure stability typical of early September along the Red Sea coast. These conditions limit cloud cover and convective cooling while allowing daytime heating to peak in the mid-afternoon, consistent with the 1991–2020 climatological average maximum of 38.3°C yet tempered by the moderating marine influence. Market-implied probabilities favor 37–38°C as the most likely recorded peak, reflecting minor model spread in exact timing and station-specific measurement thresholds rather than any abrupt synoptic shift. Updated runs in the next 24 hours will refine whether slight warming pushes the outcome toward 38°C or holds near 37°C.

eventMetadata.context_description: Enhanced southwest monsoon (habagat) driven by nearby tropical systems like Tropical Depression Pilandok is delivering persistent cloud cover, scattered thunderstorms, and high humidity across Metro Manila, suppressing peak daytime temperatures. PAGASA guidance and short-range models converge on highs near 28–29 °C (82–84 °F) for September 3, with 80–95 % rain probability and moderate-to-strong southwesterly winds limiting solar insolation. A developing moderate-to-strong El Niño adds longer-term context but exerts limited influence on this 48-hour window. Traders therefore assign higher implied probability to the lower end of the historical early-September range, as the active monsoon pattern favors reduced maxima compared with clearer climatological baselines. Updated PAGASA bulletins and model runs through September 2 remain the key near-term catalysts.
